**Complainant:** Rakesh Sharma
**Opposite Party:** Authorised Service Centre, XYZ Mobiles, Bhopal

2. The handset developed a hardware fault within warranty and was handed to the service centre.

2(7), 2(11), 39

Invoice, warranty card, service centre job sheet.

summary: Client's motorcycle worth Rs 60,000 was stolen from his hostel parking last week and the local police station refused to register the FIR. Client needs a written complaint to the SP.
draft_md:
# Complaint to Station House Officer

**To:** SHO, Police Station Kolar, Bhopal
**From:** Arjun Singh Thakur

## Facts
1. My motorcycle (reg. no. MP04-XXXX), worth Rs 60,000, was stolen from the hostel parking area on the night of 13 Sept 2026.
2. On visiting the police station, the duty officer refused to register an FIR.

## Request
Kindly register an FIR under the relevant sections of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 and investigate.

## Sections Relied
303, BNSS 173

---

# Letter to Superintendent of Police (if FIR still refused)

**To:** The Superintendent of Police, Bhopal

As the officer-in-charge at PS Kolar has refused to register my complaint of theft of motorcycle worth Rs 60,000, I am forwarding the substance of my complaint in writing under BNSS 173(4) for appropriate action, including registration of a Zero FIR if required.

## What to carry
ID proof, vehicle RC, purchase/insurance papers, this written complaint (2 copies).

Note: Zero FIR (BNSS 173(1)) can be filed at any police station regardless of jurisdiction.

# Counter-Notice to Landlord

**To:** Mr. [Landlord Name]
**From:** Ramesh Chandra Dubey, Tenant

## Facts
1. I have been a tenant at [address] on a monthly rent of Rs 8,000 since 2024.
2. You have threatened to disconnect the water and electricity supply over a disputed rent claim.

## Legal Position
Cutting off essential services during a dispute, and forfeiting the deposit without accounting, are impermissible.

## Demand
Restore/continue essential services immediately and provide an itemised account of deposit deductions, failing which I shall approach the Rent Controlling Authority/civil court.

## Rules Relied
ESSENTIAL-SERVICES, FORFEITURE, MPACA-13

# Clause Review Note

**Tenant:** Farhan Qureshi

## Flagged Clauses
1. Lease term 24 months, not registered — inadmissible as evidence of its terms and required to be registered.
2. Security deposit of 6 months' rent for a residential unit exceeds the permissible cap.
3. Penalty clause of Rs 50,000 for early exit — enforceable only to the extent of actual loss shown by the landlord.

## Next Steps
Request registration of the lease or reliance only on rent receipts; negotiate deposit down to 2 months; contest penalty clause if invoked without proof of loss.

## Rules Relied
REG-17, REG-49, MTA-11, CA-74, LOCKIN

**To:** [Landlord]
**From:** Geeta Bai Ahirwar

## Facts
1. I am a month-to-month tenant paying rent of Rs 5,000.
2. I received your notice dated 15 Sept 2026 asking me to vacate within 5 days citing bona fide personal need.

## Legal Position
A month-to-month tenancy requires at least 15 days' notice for termination, and eviction on the ground of bona fide requirement must follow the procedure before the Rent Controlling Authority, not a unilateral notice.

## Response

## Rules Relied
TPA-106, MPACA-12
